recentItems.title: Discussion | The legal implications of withdrawal of ConCourt asylum directive
recentItems.description:
The Department of Home Affairs has withdrawn its directive on accepting new asylum applications, following violent protests in Durban, Soweto, Marabastad and Gqeberha. 

The directive was issued after a Constitutional Court judgment in the Scalabrini Cape Town matter, but Home Affairs says refugee reception offices were overwhelmed, officials were placed at risk, and public safety concerns emerged. 

The department says it will now develop a new operational approach to comply with the court ruling. 

But what does the withdrawal mean for asylum seekers, constitutional rights and immigration management? 

We're joined by Princey Mthombeni, Co-founder of the South Africa Constitutional Review, and Ashraf Essop, an immigration attorney, alongside a representative from Mametlwe Sebei - Attorney for Lawyers for Human Rights and Governance Analyst, Sandile Swana. 


For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Asylum seekers | Wave of applications following ConCourt ruling
recentItems.description:
Asylum seekers are flooding Refugee Centres across the country to make their applications and the Department of Home Affairs is obliged to process these bids as a result of a binding Constitutional Court judgment.

This follows the Apex court's July judgment in Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town and Another versus Minister of Home Affairs and Others which confirmed an order of constitutional invalidity against parts of the Refugees Act.This, however, is NOT synonymous with citizenship or voting rights.

SABC News Senior Reporter Canny Maphanga explains why. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | Ramaphosa on the campiagn trail in the Free State
recentItems.description:
ANC President Cyril Ramaphosa is on a door-to-door campaign in Botshabelo in the Free State.

It's prioritising renewal, unity, responsive governance and putting people at the centre of local government. 

SABC News reporter Makgala Masiteng has more details from Botshabelo.

recentItems.title: KZN Police hunt for Eshowe supermarket triple murder suspect
recentItems.description:
KwaZulu-Natal police have launched a munhunt for a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a Boxer Superstore in Eshowe, KwaZulu-Natal. 

Reports indicate that the suspect is a former employee of the store.

Police say he had gone for an internal disciplinary hearing when he allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people.

recentItems.title: Mamelodi twins laid to rest after fatal stabbing
recentItems.description:
The funeral of 14-year-old twins Bonolo and Bothlale Makena have been laid to rest at their home in Mamelodi West. 

The teenagers were allegedly stabbed to death inside their home last week. 

Their mother reportedly discovered their bodies with multiple stab wounds when she returned from work. 

SABC News'  Thabiso Radebe reports from Mamelodi. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | ICM President Joe Mojapelo on the movement’s election plans
recentItems.description:
The Independent Citizens Movement (ICM) was founded in 2021 by professionals and religious leaders who wanted a different approach to politics and local government. 

Five years later, the movement says it has shown that even one seat in council can influence decisions, challenge poor governance and hold leaders accountable. 

As South Africa prepares for the local government elections, ICM is calling for community-driven leadership that puts residents ahead of party politics. 

But what has the movement achieved, and what does it offer voters? I am now joined by Dr Joe Mojapelo, President of the Independent Citizens Movement. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.
